title: Chlorhexidine Reduced Plaque, Gingivitis in Fixed
html:
Chlorhexidine mouthwash reduced plaque and gingival inflammation in patients wearing fixed orthodontic appliances, with the 0.2% concentration producing the clearest benefit, according to a systematic review and meta-analysis published Nov. 23 in Progress in Orthodontics.

The review included 21 randomized controlled trials, 19 of which contributed to pooled analyses. The primary analyses covered 904 patients in chlorhexidine and control groups.

At 0.2%, chlorhexidine lowered plaque index scores by a mean of 0.68 and gingival index scores by 0.69 compared with controls. At 0.12%, reductions were smaller and only borderline significant, and the gingival index result did not hold up in sensitivity analyses.

Bleeding severity improved at both concentrations. The authors found no reliable benefit for the percentage of bleeding sites, and probing depth, measured in only two trials, did not differ significantly.

Heterogeneity was high for most outcomes. Protocols varied in concentration, rinse volume, rinsing time, frequency, and duration, which ran from about two weeks to two months in most trials, and control groups ranged from placebo rinses to brushing alone. Adverse effects such as staining could not be pooled because trials reported them inconsistently, and the authors described the difference between concentrations as exploratory rather than proof that 0.2% is superior.

The review was conducted by Almiqdad I. Dashti, Abdulaziz R. Almutairi, Yousef Alomran, and colleagues, most of whom are affiliated with Kuwait’s Ministry of Health. The authors declared no competing interests.

The authors concluded that chlorhexidine is best used as a short-term adjunct for patients with inadequate plaque control or active gingivitis, within a structured oral hygiene program, rather than as a routine prescription for all orthodontic patients or a substitute for brushing and interdental cleaning.

Sources:
Progress in Orthodontics, “Chlorhexidine mouthwash for oral hygiene maintenance in orthodontic patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials,” Nov. 23, 2026: link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40510-026-00649-8
